problems.field: participants.n_analyzed; arms[].n_analyzed; eligibility.criterion_2_at_least_50_people (support for the challenged positive conclusion)
problems.source_says: The source describes 60 targeted students and assignment of 30 to each instructional arm, but gives no analyzed total or analyzed count for either arm. Neither the procedural statements about submitting final works and conducting posttests nor the pretest/posttest means establish how many distinct students entered analysis. Exclusions and attrition are not quantified, and Table 5 explicitly counts 30 works, not people. Thus the challenged conclusion that at least 50 people were analyzed lacks source support. This problem concerns that positive conclusion: the supplied final form already correctly leaves analyzed counts null and criterion 2 unclear, and its 60/30/30 assignment counts are supported as the paper's stated counts.
problems.quote:
The study targets 60 first-year non-English major university students (divided into two natural classes).
Using a quasi-experimental design, students are randomly assigned to an experimental group and a
control group (30 each).
problems.locator: PDF p. 7, section 3.2 (quoted sampling/assignment statement); p. 8, sections 3.3.3-3.5 (submission, posttests and analysis methods); pp. 11-13, sections 5.1-5.3 and Tables 2, 4 and 5 (no analyzed people denominator); pp. 17-21, Figures 1-6 (no participant flow or analyzed people count).

confirmed.statement: S1 describes 60 first-year non-English-major students, with 30 assigned to multimodal AI instruction and 30 to traditional instruction; these are people, not outputs or ratings.
Random assignment is explicitly asserted, but the same paragraph calls the design quasi-experimental and describes two natural classes; the allocation procedure is not explained.
No analyzed total, analyzed count per arm, posttest completion denominator, exclusion count, or attrition count is reported; the form correctly retains null analyzed counts.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 7-8, sections 3.2-3.5; pp. 11-14, results and conclusion; pp. 17-21, Figures 1-6. Form: studies[0].participants.n_analyzed and studies[0].arms[].n_analyzed.

confirmed.statement: Table 5 reports N = 30 works analyzed; the number of contributing students, source-specific counts, and pairing are unstated, so these works cannot establish a participant denominator.

confirmed.statement: Two teachers serve as instructors/interviewees and one technical staff member supports the platform; these roles do not add randomized creative-writing students.

confirmed.statement: The complete markdown and all 21 PDF pages were checked, including the end figures; no appendix, participant-flow diagram, or supplementary participant count is supplied.

summary: The paper describes 60 students assigned 30 per arm but never reports how many were analyzed, leaving the claim of at least 50 analyzed people unsupported. The final form correctly records the assignment counts, leaves analyzed counts null, and marks criterion 2 unclear; the challenge refutes the positive eligibility conclusion, not those cautious entries.
